# SEO-057: Declare canonicals for non-HTML documents with an HTTP Link header

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

## Statement

A PDF or other non-HTML resource that is reachable at more than one address carries its canonical declaration in a Link response header, because the format has no document head to hold a link element.

## Rationale

Without a header there is no place to express canonicalization for these resources, so duplicate copies of the same document at different addresses stay independent and compete with each other.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site",
    "public_documents"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Add the header at the layer that serves the file - object storage metadata, CDN response rules, or the download route handler - using the rel=canonical link relation with an absolute URL. Verify the header survives the CDN, which may strip unknown headers.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Request the document URL and read the Link response header, confirming it carries a rel=canonical parameter with an absolute target.
- Evidence: `HTTP_HEADER`, `HTTP_STATUS`, `FILE`
- Automated check: none.

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`
